intro: Visible patches can be easy to copy. A masked reconstruction objective evaluates only patches withheld from the encoder.
task: Return the mean squared error over masked patch features and its gradient with respect to the prediction.
requirements: prediction and target are matching batch-by-patches-by-features tensors. masked is a matching batch-by-patches numeric 0/1 matrix and must select at least one patch.
Return {"loss": scalar, "gradient": prediction-shaped tensor}. Average squared errors over all selected scalar feature values, not over all patches. Unselected gradients are zero.

Use finite real numeric values of magnitude at most 1e6, excluding boolean inputs. Each array axis has 1..64 entries and at most 65536 elements total unless a stricter bound is stated. Return NumPy arrays for array outputs, preserve caller inputs, and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

examples.name: Ignore visible errors
examples.output:
{'loss': 2.5, 'gradient': [[[1.0, 2.0], [0.0, 0.0]]]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: All patches masked
examples.output:
{'loss': 2.5, 'gradient': [[[1.0], [2.0]]]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

examples.name: Exact prediction
examples.output:
{'loss': 0.0, 'gradient': [[[0.0, 0.0]]]}
(NumPy arrays shown as lists; rounded to 12 significant digits.)

hints.title: Follow the data
hints.body: Expand the patch mask along the feature axis.

hints.title: Check the boundary
hints.body: The denominator is selected patch count multiplied by feature width.

explanation: Masking the objective changes both which residuals contribute and the normalization denominator. A batch with fewer selected patches should not reduce loss merely because more visible patches are ignored.
The gradient is twice the residual divided by the number of scored scalar features. Keeping zero gradients on unselected positions makes the restricted objective explicit.
